outcome: The 3F MIS now has ONE governed financial definition — Actual, Budget and % — that report, drill-down and the assistant all share, computed over a correct Budget-Actual join instead of ad-hoc SQL. Each source is first reduced to one ACTIVE row per (gl_code, month), so Budget no longer fans out across a GL's Actual cost centres; the two are then FULL-OUTER-joined with zero-fill, so a Budget-only or Actual-only GL still appears (valued 0.00) instead of vanishing. The % follows the confirmed nil rule in one place: blank/NA when both sides are zero, 'over-budget' when actual spend exists against no budget, and 'credit / negative actual' when that actual is a credit. Access is fail-closed at the single execution boundary — a governed-financial read action plus the domain and every selected measure and dimension grant — and row scope is applied to BOTH sources, so a user scoped away from DUB sees no DUB Budget rows. Every governed number is now explainable: the same composed query returns which sides fed each row (matched / budget-only / actual-only), the deterministic Budget-Components label set, and the ACTIVE source batch ids as (source, period, batch) tuples, with one-sided rows citing only the batch that actually contributed — so when a reload changes an answer, it is attributable to that batch swap. Correctness is frozen behind a golden-answer fixture asserting exact values for all six cases (matched, Budget-only, Actual-only, duplicate/no-fan-out, reload/active-swap, %-edges), demonstrated against a real warehouse (13/13, with a dead-port control proving the proof genuinely connects). This unblocks the MIS reporting epic: the statement, its drill-down and the assistant can now select governed measures rather than author SQL.
